evidence: tools/economy_check/test_check_tier_rule.py, witness_two_hop_decorative_gap_documented_not_fixed (run 2026-08-28): a chain with materials {topsoil, copper, byproduct}, one recipe fake_recipe(inputs=[copper], outputs=[byproduct], requires_verbs=[assay]), and demands D1 (requires topsoil, grants cut_hardness=2.0 + verb assay) and D2 (requires byproduct, grants nothing) -- check_output_consequence reports D1=pass (clause a, assay is referenced by fake_recipe) and D2=fail (grants nothing referenced anywhere, not a prerequisite of anything later), while check_terminal_products reports byproduct=pass ('required by a demand') despite that demand being D2, which itself fails. All three assertions OBSERVED passing (34/34 total cases, this run).

tools/economy_check/check_tier_rule.py, check_terminal_products: the consumed_by_demand branch is `entry['material'] for d in demands for entry in d['requires']` -- a set membership test against every demand's raw requirement, with no join back to that demand's own check_output_consequence verdict. The schema (schema.py) carries no field for one demand's derived verdict, so no such join is even representable without a design change this session did not make.
narrative: Director-confirmed and left open on purpose, not a defect to silently patch: closing this fully would mean recursively verifying that everything downstream of a verb/material reference is itself non-decorative, arbitrarily deep -- a materially larger problem than the three-part rule's stated scope, and the director's explicit instruction was 'leave it open,' not 'fix it now.' Logged as a FINDING, not folded into a DECISION, because nothing was decided here except to record the gap -- the actual decision (whether/how to close it) is deferred to whenever real economy data makes it concrete. Surfaced in the checker's own report output (RESIDUAL_NOTE, printed in every run, not just this event or the module docstring) per the director's explicit instruction that a green result must not silently exclude a verified case. The director's own framing for how this gets used: 'when the real economy is authored, this finding is the thing to check the D-chain against by hand' -- this event is what makes that possible, since a finding logged only in a chat transcript would not survive to that session.
observation: tools/economy_check/check_tier_rule.py's output-consequence check (clause a: a granted verb counts if some Recipe.requires_verbs names it; clause b: an opened material counts if it is in schema.meaningfully_referenced_materials, i.e. a recipe input or the breach) verifies exactly ONE HOP of 'meaningfully referenced.' It does not verify that the recipe consuming the verb, or the demand consuming an opened material, is itself non-decorative. Concretely: a demand D1 granting verb V, referenced only by Recipe R, whose sole output is required only by demand D2, PASSES via clause (a) even when D2 independently FAILS output consequence (grants nothing referenced anywhere, is not a prerequisite of anything). check_terminal_products compounds this: its consumed_by_demand branch treats 'required by any demand' as sufficient consumption, with no check on whether that consuming demand itself passed anything -- so the recipe's output is never flagged terminal either, even though the whole chain past D1 terminates in something decorative.
